import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Adelic.BoundedVanishing
set_option autoImplicit false
universe u
open AlgebraicGeometry Adelic
variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)

/-- `hle` of `ell_le_ell_add_residueDeg` is derivable from `hstep` + `hoff`. -/
theorem probe_hle_redundant {D D' : X.WeilDivisor} {P : X.PrimeDivisor}
    (hstep : (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P =
      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P + 1)
    (hoff : ∀ Q : X.PrimeDivisor, Q ≠ P →
      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q = (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') Q) :
    ∀ Q : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q ≤
      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') Q := by
  intro Q
  rcases eq_or_ne Q P with rfl | h
  · omega
  · rw [hoff Q h]

/-- `hpeel` of the main theorem does NOT imply `hbase`: at `D' = D₀` it is trivially
true with `y = x`, for ANY divisor and any cover.  So the instance of `hpeel` at
`D₀` carries no information. -/
theorem probe_hpeel_at_base (D₀ : X.WeilDivisor) :
    ∀ x ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D₀, ∃ y ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D₀,
      x - y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D₀ :=
  fun x hx => ⟨x, hx, by simp⟩
EOF

309	The **closed ledger** is the identity `χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D` for every Weil

313	connecting/surjectivity data plus the strong-approximation input `hsurj`.  So the
314	statements below take the closed ledger as an explicit hypothesis, spelled
315	exactly as it will be discharged:
316	
317	`hledger : ∀ D, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D`.
318

321	missing. -/

324	
325	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
326	    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
327	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
328	
329	/-- **The ledger holds on list-effective divisors, given the one-point bump.**
330	`chi_telescope_list` computes `χ(Σ_{P ∈ L} P)` as `χ(0) + Σ_{P ∈ L} deg P`, and
331	`degK_divisorOfList` computes `deg_k` of the same divisor as the same sum, so the
332	two agree: `χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D` for `D = divisorOfList L`.
333	
334	This is what pins `degK` as *the* degree of the ledger rather than one weighting
335	among several, and it shows the `hledger` hypothesis of this section is not
336	idle — it holds wherever the one-point bump `hbump` does, which is one application
337	of `chi_add_eq_residueDeg` per step.  What `hbump` still costs is the ledger's
338	connecting/surjectivity data plus the strong-approximation input, and extending
339	from list-effective divisors to *all* divisors additionally needs the negative
340	part; both are why the general ledger is a hypothesis and not a theorem here. -/
341	theorem chi_divisorOfList_eq_degK (L : List X.PrimeDivisor)
342	    (hbump : ∀ (P : X.PrimeDivisor) (E : X.WeilDivisor),
343	      chi k U₀ U₁ (pointDivisor P + E) = chi k U₀ U₁ E + residueDeg k P) :
344	    chi k U₀ U₁ (divisorOfList L) =
345	      chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k (divisorOfList L : X.WeilDivisor) := by
346	  rw [chi_telescope_list k U₀ U₁ L hbump, degK_divisorOfList]
347	
348	/-- **The Riemann inequality in closed weighted form.**  Given the closed ledger,
349	`deg_k D + χ(0) ≤ ℓ(D)` for every `D` — the `h¹ ≥ 0` half applied to the
350	telescoped Euler characteristic.  (This is `Adelic.riemann_inequality` with its
351	`htel` hypothesis supplied from the ledger and the degree pinned to the
352	residue-weighted `deg_k`.) -/
353	theorem degK_add_chi_zero_le_ell
354	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
355	    (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
356	    degK k D + chi k U₀ U₁ 0 ≤ (ell k D : ℤ) :=
357	  riemann_inequality k U₀ U₁ (hledger D)
358	
359	end Ledger
360	
361	section LedgerNoetherian
362	
363	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
364	    [IsNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
365	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
366	
367	/-- **`deg_k D < 0 ⟹ ℓ(D) = 0`** (campaign P4(a)).  Given the closed ledger: a
368	nonzero `f ∈ L(D)` would make `D` linearly equivalent to an effective divisor
369	`E = D + div f` (`exists_effective_linearEquiv_of_ne_zero_mem`); `χ` is a
370	class invariant (`chi_eq_of_linearEquivalence`), so the ledger forces
371	`deg_k E = deg_k D < 0`, contradicting `deg_k E ≥ 0` for effective `E`
372	(`degK_nonneg_of_nonneg`).
373	
374	Note the shape: the hypothesis is on `deg_k`, the *weighted* degree, and the
375	argument runs entirely through the class-invariance of `χ` — no vanishing input,
376	no duality. -/
377	theorem ell_eq_zero_of_degK_neg
378	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
379	    {D : X.WeilDivisor} (hdeg : degK k D < 0)
380	    [Module.Finite k (sectionSub k ⊤ D)] :
381	    ell k D = 0 := by
382	  by_contra hne
383	  -- a nonzero section exists
384	  obtain ⟨f, hfmem, hfne⟩ : ∃ f : X.functionField, f ∈ sectionSub k ⊤ D ∧ f ≠ 0 := by
385	    by_contra hno
386	    have hbot : sectionSub k ⊤ D = ⊥ := by
387	      apply le_antisymm _ bot_le
388	      intro x hx
389	      rcases eq_or_ne x 0 with rfl | hx0
390	      · exact Submodule.zero_mem _
391	      · exact absurd ⟨x, hx, hx0⟩ hno
392	    rw [ell, hbot] at hne
393	    simp at hne
394	  obtain ⟨E, hEnonneg, hEclass⟩ :=
395	    exists_effective_linearEquiv_of_ne_zero_mem hfne hfmem
396	  have hchi := chi_eq_of_linearEquivalence k U₀ U₁ hEclass
397	  rw [hledger E, hledger D] at hchi
398	  have : degK k E = degK k D := by omega
399	  have hEpos := degK_nonneg_of_nonneg k hEnonneg
400	  omega
401	
402	/-- **Principal divisors have residue-weighted degree zero** — the adelic
403	counterpart of the geometric statement `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero`.
404	
405	Given the closed ledger, this is a two-line consequence of the class-invariance of
406	`χ` proved in `ClassInvariance.lean`: `0 − div g` is in the class of `0`, so
407	`χ(0 − div g) = χ(0)`, and the ledger reads off
408	`deg_k (0 − div g) = 0`, i.e. `deg_k (div g) = 0`.
409	
410	This is the *weighted* statement.  It does **not** close the open geometric leaf
411	`principal_degree_zero`, which asserts the same for the unweighted degree
412	`Σ_P ord_P g`; see §4. -/
413	theorem degK_principal_eq_zero
414	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
415	    {g : X.functionField} (hg : g ≠ 0) :
416	    degK k (Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg) = 0 := by
417	  have hchi := chi_eq_of_principal_shift k U₀ U₁ (0 : X.WeilDivisor) hg
418	  rw [hledger ((0 : X.WeilDivisor) - Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg),
419	    hledger (0 : X.WeilDivisor), degK_sub, degK_zero] at hchi
420	  omega
421	
422	/-- **`deg_k` descends to linear-equivalence classes.**  Given the closed ledger,
423	linearly equivalent divisors have equal weighted degree — the well-definedness
424	statement the Picard route consumes when it needs "the degree of a class". -/
425	theorem degK_eq_of_linearEquivalence
426	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
427	    {D D' : X.WeilDivisor} (h : Scheme.WeilDivisor.LinearEquivalence D D') :
428	    degK k D = degK k D' := by
429	  have hchi := chi_eq_of_linearEquivalence k U₀ U₁ h
430	  rw [hledger D, hledger D'] at hchi
431	  omega
432	
433	end LedgerNoetherian
434	
435	section GeometricDegree
436	
437	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
438	    [IsNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
439	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
440	
441	/-- **The geometric principal-degree-zero statement, reduced to residue degree
442	one.**  `Σ_P ord_P(g) = 0` follows from the closed ledger together with
443	`[κ(P):k] = 1` on the support of `div g`.
444	
445	This makes the reduction of the open leaf `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero`
446	machine-checked rather than merely asserted: the *whole* remaining content of that
447	leaf, given the ledger, is the residue-degree-one fact for a smooth proper curve
448	over an algebraically closed field.  It is stated here on the adelic hypotheses
449	(`Algebra k K(X)`, `IsConstantField`, a 2-affine cover, the ledger) rather than on
450	the leaf's own geometric hypotheses, which is why it does not literally close that
451	`sorry` — the missing step is instantiating these hypotheses from
452	`[IsProper] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1] [GeometricallyIrreducible]` over `k̄`,
453	together with `residueDeg k̄ P = 1`. -/
454	theorem degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one
455	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
456	    {g : X.functionField} (hg : g ≠ 0)
457	    (h1 : ∀ P ∈ (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from
458	      Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg).support, residueDeg k P = 1) :
459	    Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree (Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg) = 0 := by
460	  rw [← degK_eq_degree_of_residueDeg_eq_one k h1]
461	  exact degK_principal_eq_zero k U₀ U₁ hledger hg
462	
463	end GeometricDegree
464	
465	/-! ## §4. `degK_principal_eq_zero` versus the geometric `principal_degree_zero`
466	
467	`degK_principal_eq_zero` above and the open leaf
468	`Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero` are **different statements**, and the
469	first does not imply the second.  Recorded here because the difference is easy to
470	misread as a formality.
471	
472	* `degK_principal_eq_zero` concerns `deg_k (div g) = Σ_P ord_P(g)·[κ(P):k]`.  Its
473	  proof is the χ-transport of `ClassInvariance.lean` plus the closed ledger, and
474	  it is stated over an **arbitrary** base field of constants `k`.
475	* `principal_degree_zero` concerns the **unweighted** `Σ_P ord_P(g)`, and is
476	  stated on a smooth proper curve over an algebraically **closed** `k̄` with no
477	  field of constants in sight and no ledger hypothesis.
478	
479	Over `k̄` the two degrees coincide because every closed point of a smooth curve has
480	residue field `k̄`, i.e. `[κ(P):k̄] = 1`.  That collapse is
481	`degK_eq_degree_of_residueDeg_eq_one`, and composing it with
482	`degK_principal_eq_zero` gives `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one`:
483	the **unweighted** statement, proved, from the ledger plus residue-degree-one.
484	
485	So the reduction is now machine-checked, and the residue of the open leaf is
486	exactly two items, neither of them about divisor theory:
487	
488	1. `residueDeg k̄ P = 1` for every prime divisor `P` of a smooth proper curve over
489	   an algebraically closed `k̄` — a statement about residue fields of closed
490	   points (`κ(P)` is a finite extension of `k̄`, hence `k̄`);
491	2. the instance plumbing that places `principal_degree_zero`'s own geometric
492	   hypotheses in adelic shape: an `Algebra k̄ K(C)` with
493	   `IsConstantField k̄ C.left` (available — `Adelic/GateInstances.lean`), a
494	   2-affine cover, and the closed ledger for that cover.
495	
496	The `sorry` in `WeilDivisor.lean` is deliberately **left in place**.  Replacing it
497	with a call to `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one` would require
498	producing the ledger for a cover of `C`, and the ledger is itself not yet a
499	theorem here (see §3) — so the substitution would move the gap rather than close
500	it, while making a theorem whose statement mentions no hypotheses depend silently
501	on one.  The Hartshorne II.6.10 route sketched in that docstring (build
502	`φ : C → ℙ¹` from `g`, use multiplicativity of degree under finite pullback) is a
503	*different*, heavier proof; the ledger route above is the cheaper one and is what
504	the campaign's P3 milestone anticipated. -/
505	
506	end Adelic
507	end AlgebraicGeometry

`div(f⁻¹) = -div(f)`, transitivity from `div(fg) = div(f) + div(g)`, all via
`thm:principal_hom`). The quotient `Cl(X) := Div(X) / im(div)` is the
**divisor class group** of `X`.

On a smooth proper curve `C` over `k̄`, `thm:principal_deg_zero` shows the
degree map descends to `deg : Cl(C) → ℤ`.

Blueprint reference: `def:linear_equivalence` (Hartshorne II §6 p. 131). -/
def LinearEquivalence [IsIntegral X] [IsNoetherian X]
    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X] (D D' : X.WeilDivisor) : Prop :=
  ∃ (f : X.functionField) (hf : f ≠ 0), D - D' = principal f hf

end Scheme.WeilDivisor

end AlgebraicGeometry

8	/-!
9	# Adelic Riemann–Roch — bounded `H¹` vanishing over a single base field
10	
11	This file assembles the **single-field bounded vanishing** statement of the
12	campaign's cluster P (P5, primary clause):
13	
14	`∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D, b ≤ deg_k D → Subsingleton (Ȟ¹(D))`
15	
16	from three inputs that are named explicitly in every statement:
17	
18	1. **a base vanishing** `Subsingleton (Ȟ¹(D₀))` at one divisor `D₀`;
19	2. **the peel input** — surjectivity of the twist `Ȟ¹(D) ↠ Ȟ¹(D')` for `D ≤ D'`,
20	   in the concrete form `𝒜(D') = 𝒜(D) + B(D')`.  This is exactly the `htwist`
21	   datum of the χ-ledger (`chi_add`), unwound;
22	3. **the closed ledger** `χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D`, used only to produce an
23	   effective witness in the class of `D − D₀`.
24	
25	Nothing here is a `sorry` and nothing here is a new gate class: each theorem is of
26	the form "given (1)–(3), the bound exists", with `b` computed explicitly as
27	`b = deg_k D₀ + 1 − χ(0)`.
28	
29	## Vanishing as `Subsingleton`, not as `h¹ = 0`
30	
31	Vanishing is stated as `Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D)` rather than
32	`h1dim k U₀ U₁ D = 0`.  The two agree when `Ȟ¹(D)` is finite-dimensional, but the
33	`Subsingleton` form needs **no finiteness instance**, so the vanishing lane stays
34	independent of the finiteness gates.  `h1dim_eq_zero_of_subsingleton` converts.
35	
36	## Main declarations
37	
38	* `subsingleton_h1Mod_iff` — `Ȟ¹(D) = 0 ⟺ 𝒜(D) ⊆ B(D)`: the concrete criterion
39	  everything below runs on.
40	* `subsingleton_h1Mod_peel` — the **peel step**: base vanishing at `D` plus the
41	  peel input transports vanishing to any `D' ≥ D`.
42	* `subsingleton_h1Mod_of_linearEquivalence` — vanishing is a class invariant
43	  (from `ClassInvariance.lean`, finiteness-free).
44	* `exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod` — the assembled bound.
45	
46	## Relation to the sibling project's `UniformVanishing.lean`
47	
48	`AJCR RiemannRoch/UniformVanishing.lean` proves a statement of exactly this
49	shape, `∃ b, ∀ D, b ≤ deg D → Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(D))`, and its proof has the same
50	skeleton: fix a base twist, produce an effective witness of the residual class,
51	peel it, transport along the class.  **This file is not a port of it.**  AJCR's
52	version obtains its base vanishing from the FLV-class machine
53	(`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean`, via a finite dominant `π : Y → ℙ¹` and the fiber
54	divisor) and its peel step from `peel_effective` on `divisorSheaf`; neither the
55	FLV machinery nor `divisorSheaf` exists in AJC.  So here (1) and (2) are named
56	hypotheses rather than discharged lemmas, and the file is honest about that: what
57	is *new* relative to AJC is the assembly and the class-transport, and those are
58	now proved.
59	
60	## The three gaps, kept apart
61	
62	`exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod` is **single-field**: `k`, the cover `U₀, U₁` and
63	the base divisor `D₀` are all fixed.  It is therefore strictly weaker than the two
64	things downstream consumers eventually want, and neither is proved anywhere in
65	this project:
66	
67	* **extension uniformity** — the *same* `b` for every field extension `κ/k`.
68	  Needs flat base change of the bound along `k → κ`; nothing here quantifies over
69	  extensions, and note that even the *statement* needs the base-changed cover

112	  · intro hle
113	    constructor
114	    intro a b
115	    obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ a
116	    obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ b

120	/-- **The peel step.**  Suppose `Ȟ¹(D)` vanishes and the twist `Ȟ¹(D) → Ȟ¹(D')`
121	is surjective — concretely, every overlap section of `𝒪(D')` agrees, modulo the
122	coboundary `B(D')`, with an overlap section of `𝒪(D)`.  Then `Ȟ¹(D')` vanishes.
123	
124	`D'` is typically `D + E` with `E ≥ 0`: this is "peel off an effective divisor",

126	`hpeel` hypothesis is the ledger's surjectivity datum `htwist`, unwound; it is
127	supplied here as a hypothesis because AJC has no unconditional source for it. -/
128	theorem subsingleton_h1Mod_peel {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
129	    (hbase : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D))
130	    (hpeel : ∀ x ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D', ∃ y ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D,
131	      x - y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D')
132	    (hle : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P ≤
133	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) :
134	    Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D') := by
135	  rw [subsingleton_h1Mod_iff] at hbase ⊢
136	  intro x hx
137	  obtain ⟨y, hy, hxy⟩ := hpeel x hx
138	  have hyB : y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D' := by
139	    have : y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D := hbase hy
140	    exact coboundarySub_mono k U₀ U₁ hle this
141	  have : x = (x - y) + y := by abel
142	  rw [this]
143	  exact (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D').add_mem hxy hyB
144	
145	/-- **The peel relation `Peel D D'`.**  "Every overlap section of `𝒪(D')` agrees,
146	modulo the coboundary `B(D')`, with an overlap section of `𝒪(D)`" — equivalently,
147	the twist `Ȟ¹(D) → Ȟ¹(D')` is surjective.  Named so that it can be composed
148	(`Peel.trans`) and so that consumers can discharge it one point at a time rather
149	than in one step. -/
150	def Peel (D D' : X.WeilDivisor) : Prop :=
151	  ∀ x ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D', ∃ y ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D,
152	    x - y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D'

154	/-- **The peel relation is reflexive** (take `y = x`). -/
155	theorem Peel.refl (D : X.WeilDivisor) : Peel k U₀ U₁ D D :=
156	  fun x hx => ⟨x, hx, by simp⟩
157	
158	/-- **The peel relation composes.**  `Peel D₀ D₁` and `Peel D₁ D₂` give
159	`Peel D₀ D₂`, provided `D₁ ≤ D₂` (so that `B(D₁) ⊆ B(D₂)`).

164	analogue of AJCR's `peel_effective`, which peels a whole effective divisor in one
165	sheaf-level step. -/
166	theorem Peel.trans {D₀ D₁ D₂ : X.WeilDivisor}
167	    (h₀₁ : Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ D₁) (h₁₂ : Peel k U₀ U₁ D₁ D₂)
168	    (hle : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₁) P ≤
169	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₂) P) :
170	    Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ D₂ := by
171	  intro x hx
172	  obtain ⟨y, hy, hxy⟩ := h₁₂ x hx
173	  obtain ⟨z, hz, hyz⟩ := h₀₁ y hy
174	  refine ⟨z, hz, ?_⟩
175	  have : x - z = (x - y) + (y - z) := by abel
176	  rw [this]
177	  exact (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D₂).add_mem hxy
178	    (coboundarySub_mono k U₀ U₁ hle hyz)

180	/-- **Chaining one-point peels along a list.**  If every one-point bump peels —
181	`Peel E (1·P + E)` for every prime divisor `P` and every `E` — then `D₀` peels to
182	`divisorOfList L + D₀` for every list `L`, i.e. to `D₀` plus an arbitrary effective
183	divisor.  Induction on `L` with `Peel.trans`. -/
184	theorem Peel.of_list (hstep : ∀ (P : X.PrimeDivisor) (E : X.WeilDivisor),
185	      Peel k U₀ U₁ E (pointDivisor P + E))
186	    (D₀ : X.WeilDivisor) (L : List X.PrimeDivisor) :
187	    Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ (divisorOfList L + D₀) := by
188	  induction L with
189	  | nil =>
190	    have h0 : divisorOfList ([] : List X.PrimeDivisor) + D₀ = D₀ := by
191	      rw [divisorOfList, zero_add]
192	    rw [h0]
193	    exact Peel.refl k U₀ U₁ D₀
194	  | cons P L ih =>
195	    have hassoc : divisorOfList (P :: L) + D₀ =
196	        pointDivisor P + (divisorOfList L + D₀) := by
197	      rw [divisorOfList]; abel
198	    rw [hassoc]
199	    refine ih.trans k U₀ U₁ (hstep P (divisorOfList L + D₀)) fun Q => ?_
200	    exact le_add_pointDivisor (divisorOfList L + D₀) P Q
201	
202	/-- **Vanishing is a linear-equivalence invariant** (finiteness-free).  The
203	multiplication isomorphism of `ClassInvariance.lean` is a `k`-linear isomorphism
204	`Ȟ¹(D) ≃ₗ[k] Ȟ¹(D')` whenever `D' = D − div g`, and `Subsingleton` transports
205	along any equivalence. -/
206	theorem subsingleton_h1Mod_of_shift {D D' : X.WeilDivisor} {g : X.functionField}
207	    (hg : g ≠ 0)
208	    (hD' : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P =
209	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P - Scheme.RationalMap.order P g)
210	    (h : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D)) :
211	    Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D') :=
212	  (h1ModMulEquiv k U₀ U₁ hg hD').symm.toEquiv.subsingleton
213	
214	/-- **`h¹ = 0` from vanishing**, for consumers phrased on the numerical
215	invariant. -/
216	theorem h1dim_eq_zero_of_subsingleton {D : X.WeilDivisor}
217	    (h : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D)) : h1dim k U₀ U₁ D = 0 := by
218	  rw [h1dim]
219	  exact Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton
220	
221	end Vanishing

223	/-! ## §2. The assembled single-field bound
224	
225	The assembly.  Fix a base divisor `D₀` with `Ȟ¹(D₀) = 0`.  For `D` of large
226	weighted degree the residual class `D − D₀` has `χ ≥ 1`, hence a nonzero global
227	section, hence an **effective** representative `E ~ D − D₀` (the effective-witness
228	dictionary of `ClassInvariance.lean`).  Then `D₀ + E ≥ D₀`, so peeling `E` off the
229	base vanishing kills `Ȟ¹(D₀ + E)`, and `D₀ + E ~ D` transports it to `Ȟ¹(D)`.
230	
231	The threshold that makes the residual class have a section is
232	`b := deg_k D₀ + 1 − χ(0)`: for `deg_k D ≥ b` the ledger gives
233	`χ(D − D₀) = χ(0) + deg_k D − deg_k D₀ ≥ 1`, and `χ ≤ ℓ` does the rest.

238	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]

244	`Γ(⊤, 𝒪(D)) ≠ 0`. -/
245	theorem exists_ne_zero_mem_of_one_le_chi {D : X.WeilDivisor}
246	    (hchi : 1 ≤ chi k U₀ U₁ D) :
247	    ∃ f : X.functionField, f ∈ sectionSub k ⊤ D ∧ f ≠ 0 := by
248	  have hell : 1 ≤ (ell k D : ℤ) := le_trans hchi (chi_le_ell k U₀ U₁ D)
249	  by_contra hno
250	  have hbot : sectionSub k ⊤ D = ⊥ := by
251	    apply le_antisymm _ bot_le
252	    intro x hx
253	    rcases eq_or_ne x 0 with rfl | hx0
254	    · exact Submodule.zero_mem _
255	    · exact absurd ⟨x, hx, hx0⟩ hno
256	  rw [ell, hbot] at hell
257	  simp at hell

265	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
266	    {D : X.WeilDivisor} (hdeg : 1 - chi k U₀ U₁ 0 ≤ degK k D) :
267	    ∃ E : X.WeilDivisor,
268	      (∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, 0 ≤ (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E) P) ∧
269	        Scheme.WeilDivisor.LinearEquivalence E D := by
270	  have hchi : 1 ≤ chi k U₀ U₁ D := by rw [hledger D]; omega
271	  obtain ⟨f, hfmem, hfne⟩ := exists_ne_zero_mem_of_one_le_chi k U₀ U₁ hchi

275	strongest form reachable in AJC today).

277	Given

279	* the **peel input** at `D₀`: for every `D' ≥ D₀`, each overlap section of
280	  `𝒪(D')` agrees modulo `B(D')` with an overlap section of `𝒪(D₀)` — i.e. the
281	  twist `Ȟ¹(D₀) → Ȟ¹(D')` is surjective (the ledger's `htwist` datum, unwound),

291	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
292	    (D₀ : X.WeilDivisor) (hbase : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D₀))
293	    (hpeel : ∀ D' : X.WeilDivisor,
294	      (∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₀) P ≤
295	        (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) →
296	      ∀ x ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D', ∃ y ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D₀,

298	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, b ≤ degK k D →
299	      Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D) := by
300	  refine ⟨degK k D₀ + 1 - chi k U₀ U₁ 0, fun D hD => ?_⟩
301	  -- the residual class `D - D₀` has weighted degree ≥ 1 - χ(0), so it is effective
302	  obtain ⟨E, hEnonneg, hEclass⟩ :=

304	      (D := D - D₀) (by rw [degK_sub]; omega)
305	  -- `D₀ + E ≥ D₀`, so peeling `E` off the base vanishing kills `Ȟ¹(D₀ + E)`

/-- **The local step `k`-vector space `Γ(U, 𝒪(D')) ⧸ Γ(U, 𝒪(D))`.** The relative
quotient of the two section subspaces; this is `ℓ(D')/ℓ(D)`-space whose dimension
the χ-ledger telescopes. -/
abbrev localStepDom (U : X.Opens) (D D' : X.WeilDivisor) : Type u :=
  ↥(sectionSub k U D') ⧸ Submodule.comap (sectionSub k U D').subtype (sectionSub k U D)

/-- **The single-point valuation subquotient `orderGe P (m-1) ⧸ orderGe P m`.**
By the DVR structure at `P` this one-uniformizer-step quotient is a copy of the
residue field `κ(P) = 𝒪_P/𝔪_P` (antitone convention: `orderGe P m ⊆ orderGe P (m-1)`). -/
abbrev localStepTgt (P : X.PrimeDivisor) (m : ℤ) : Type u :=
  ↥(orderGeSub k P (m - 1)) ⧸
    Submodule.comap (orderGeSub k P (m - 1)).subtype (orderGeSub k P m)

/-- **The `k`-linear local step map.** The `k`-linear upgrade of `localStepQuot`:
induced by the inclusion `Γ(U, 𝒪(D')) ⊆ orderGe P (-D(P)-1)` on the relative
quotients, mapping the local step subquotient
`Γ(U, 𝒪(D')) ⧸ Γ(U, 𝒪(D))` `k`-linearly into `orderGe P (-D(P)-1) ⧸ orderGe P (-D(P))`. -/
noncomputable def localStepMapₖ {U : X.Opens} {P : X.PrimeDivisor}
    (hPU : P.point ∈ U) {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
    (hstep : (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P =
      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P + 1) :
    localStepDom k U D D' →ₗ[k]
      localStepTgt k P (-(show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P) :=
  Submodule.mapQ _ _
    (Submodule.inclusion (fun x hx => sectionOfDivisor_le_orderGe hPU hstep hx)) (by
      intro g hg
      rw [Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply, mem_sectionSub] at hg
      rw [Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply,
        Submodule.coe_inclusion, mem_orderGeSub]
      rcases eq_or_ne (g : X.functionField) 0 with h0 | h0

1	/-

3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Adelic.SectionBounds
7	
8	/-!
9	# Adelic Riemann–Roch — bounded `H¹` vanishing over a single base field
10	
11	This file assembles the **single-field bounded vanishing** statement of the
12	campaign's cluster P (P5, primary clause):
13	
14	`∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D, b ≤ deg_k D → Subsingleton (Ȟ¹(D))`
15	
16	from three inputs that are named explicitly in every statement:
17	
18	1. **a base vanishing** `Subsingleton (Ȟ¹(D₀))` at one divisor `D₀`;
19	2. **the peel input** — surjectivity of the twist `Ȟ¹(D) ↠ Ȟ¹(D')` for `D ≤ D'`,
20	   in the concrete form `𝒜(D') = 𝒜(D) + B(D')`.  This is exactly the `htwist`
21	   datum of the χ-ledger (`chi_add`), unwound;
22	3. **the closed ledger** `χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D`, used only to produce an
23	   effective witness in the class of `D − D₀`.
24	
25	Nothing here is a `sorry` and nothing here is a new gate class: each theorem is of
26	the form "given (1)–(3), the bound exists", with `b` computed explicitly as
27	`b = deg_k D₀ + 1 − χ(0)`.
28	
29	## Vanishing as `Subsingleton`, not as `h¹ = 0`
30	
31	Vanishing is stated as `Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D)` rather than
32	`h1dim k U₀ U₁ D = 0`.  The two agree when `Ȟ¹(D)` is finite-dimensional, but the
33	`Subsingleton` form needs **no finiteness instance**, so the vanishing lane stays
34	independent of the finiteness gates.  `h1dim_eq_zero_of_subsingleton` converts.
35	
36	## Main declarations
37	
38	* `subsingleton_h1Mod_iff` — `Ȟ¹(D) = 0 ⟺ 𝒜(D) ⊆ B(D)`: the concrete criterion
39	  everything below runs on.
40	* `subsingleton_h1Mod_peel` — the **peel step**: base vanishing at `D` plus the
41	  peel input transports vanishing to any `D' ≥ D`.
42	* `subsingleton_h1Mod_of_linearEquivalence` — vanishing is a class invariant
43	  (from `ClassInvariance.lean`, finiteness-free).
44	* `exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod` — the assembled bound.
45	
46	## Relation to the sibling project's `UniformVanishing.lean`
47	
48	`AJCR RiemannRoch/UniformVanishing.lean` proves a statement of exactly this
49	shape, `∃ b, ∀ D, b ≤ deg D → Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(D))`, and its proof has the same
50	skeleton: fix a base twist, produce an effective witness of the residual class,
51	peel it, transport along the class.  **This file is not a port of it.**  AJCR's
52	version obtains its base vanishing from the FLV-class machine
53	(`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean`, via a finite dominant `π : Y → ℙ¹` and the fiber
54	divisor) and its peel step from `peel_effective` on `divisorSheaf`; neither the
55	FLV machinery nor `divisorSheaf` exists in AJC.  So here (1) and (2) are named
56	hypotheses rather than discharged lemmas, and the file is honest about that: what
57	is *new* relative to AJC is the assembly and the class-transport, and those are
58	now proved.
59	
60	## The three gaps, kept apart
61	
62	`exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod` is **single-field**: `k`, the cover `U₀, U₁` and
63	the base divisor `D₀` are all fixed.  It is therefore strictly weaker than the two
64	things downstream consumers eventually want, and neither is proved anywhere in
65	this project:
66	
67	* **extension uniformity** — the *same* `b` for every field extension `κ/k`.
68	  Needs flat base change of the bound along `k → κ`; nothing here quantifies over
69	  extensions, and note that even the *statement* needs the base-changed cover
70	  (`RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean` supplies `C_κ` as an AJC curve, but not the
71	  transported 2-affine cover data on which `Ȟ¹` here is pinned).
72	* **global generation** above the bound.  Needs `Ȟ¹(D − x) = 0` at every closed
73	  point `x`, i.e. the bound raised by the maximal residue degree, plus the
74	  evaluation-surjectivity argument.  Not addressed.
75	
76	`ajc-gate` should therefore not read this file as discharging a global-generation
77	or extension-uniform hypothesis; it discharges the single-field bounded-vanishing
78	shape only, and only relative to (1)–(3).
79	-/
80	
81	set_option autoImplicit false
82	
83	universe u
84	
85	open CategoryTheory Limits IsDedekindDomain
86	open scoped WithZero
87	
88	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
89	namespace Adelic
90	
91	section Vanishing
92	
93	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
94	    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
95	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
96	
97	/-- **The concrete vanishing criterion.**  `Ȟ¹(D) = 𝒜(D)/B(D)` is trivial exactly
98	when the overlap sections are already coboundaries: `𝒜(D) ⊆ B(D)`.  (The reverse
99	inclusion always holds, `coboundarySub_le_overlap`, so the condition really is
100	equality.) -/
101	theorem subsingleton_h1Mod_iff (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
102	    Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D) ↔
103	      sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D ≤ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D := by
104	  constructor
105	  · intro hsub x hx
106	    have hzero : Submodule.Quotient.mk (p := Submodule.comap
107	        (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D).subtype (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D))
108	        (⟨x, hx⟩ : sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
109	    rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero, Submodule.mem_comap,
110	      Submodule.subtype_apply] at hzero
111	    exact hzero
112	  · intro hle
113	    constructor
114	    intro a b
115	    obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ a
116	    obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ b
117	    rw [Submodule.Quotient.eq, Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply]
118	    exact hle ((sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D).sub_mem x.2 y.2)
119	
120	/-- **The peel step.**  Suppose `Ȟ¹(D)` vanishes and the twist `Ȟ¹(D) → Ȟ¹(D')`
121	is surjective — concretely, every overlap section of `𝒪(D')` agrees, modulo the
122	coboundary `B(D')`, with an overlap section of `𝒪(D)`.  Then `Ȟ¹(D')` vanishes.
123	
124	`D'` is typically `D + E` with `E ≥ 0`: this is "peel off an effective divisor",
125	the step that turns one base vanishing into vanishing on a whole cone.  The
126	`hpeel` hypothesis is the ledger's surjectivity datum `htwist`, unwound; it is
127	supplied here as a hypothesis because AJC has no unconditional source for it. -/
128	theorem subsingleton_h1Mod_peel {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
129	    (hbase : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D))
130	    (hpeel : ∀ x ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D', ∃ y ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D,
131	      x - y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D')
132	    (hle : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P ≤
133	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) :
134	    Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D') := by
135	  rw [subsingleton_h1Mod_iff] at hbase ⊢
136	  intro x hx
137	  obtain ⟨y, hy, hxy⟩ := hpeel x hx
138	  have hyB : y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D' := by
139	    have : y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D := hbase hy
140	    exact coboundarySub_mono k U₀ U₁ hle this
141	  have : x = (x - y) + y := by abel
142	  rw [this]
143	  exact (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D').add_mem hxy hyB
144	
145	/-- **The peel relation `Peel D D'`.**  "Every overlap section of `𝒪(D')` agrees,
146	modulo the coboundary `B(D')`, with an overlap section of `𝒪(D)`" — equivalently,
147	the twist `Ȟ¹(D) → Ȟ¹(D')` is surjective.  Named so that it can be composed
148	(`Peel.trans`) and so that consumers can discharge it one point at a time rather
149	than in one step. -/
150	def Peel (D D' : X.WeilDivisor) : Prop :=
151	  ∀ x ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D', ∃ y ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D,
152	    x - y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D'
153	
154	/-- **The peel relation is reflexive** (take `y = x`). -/
155	theorem Peel.refl (D : X.WeilDivisor) : Peel k U₀ U₁ D D :=
156	  fun x hx => ⟨x, hx, by simp⟩
157	
158	/-- **The peel relation composes.**  `Peel D₀ D₁` and `Peel D₁ D₂` give
159	`Peel D₀ D₂`, provided `D₁ ≤ D₂` (so that `B(D₁) ⊆ B(D₂)`).
160	
161	This is what makes the peel hypothesis of `exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod`
162	tractable: it need only be established for **one-point** bumps `E ↦ E + P`, then
163	chained along an effective divisor.  Chaining one-point peels is the adelic
164	analogue of AJCR's `peel_effective`, which peels a whole effective divisor in one
165	sheaf-level step. -/
166	theorem Peel.trans {D₀ D₁ D₂ : X.WeilDivisor}
167	    (h₀₁ : Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ D₁) (h₁₂ : Peel k U₀ U₁ D₁ D₂)
168	    (hle : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₁) P ≤
169	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₂) P) :
170	    Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ D₂ := by
171	  intro x hx
172	  obtain ⟨y, hy, hxy⟩ := h₁₂ x hx
173	  obtain ⟨z, hz, hyz⟩ := h₀₁ y hy
174	  refine ⟨z, hz, ?_⟩
175	  have : x - z = (x - y) + (y - z) := by abel
176	  rw [this]
177	  exact (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D₂).add_mem hxy
178	    (coboundarySub_mono k U₀ U₁ hle hyz)
179	
180	/-- **Chaining one-point peels along a list.**  If every one-point bump peels —
181	`Peel E (1·P + E)` for every prime divisor `P` and every `E` — then `D₀` peels to
182	`divisorOfList L + D₀` for every list `L`, i.e. to `D₀` plus an arbitrary effective
183	divisor.  Induction on `L` with `Peel.trans`. -/
184	theorem Peel.of_list (hstep : ∀ (P : X.PrimeDivisor) (E : X.WeilDivisor),
185	      Peel k U₀ U₁ E (pointDivisor P + E))
186	    (D₀ : X.WeilDivisor) (L : List X.PrimeDivisor) :
187	    Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ (divisorOfList L + D₀) := by
188	  induction L with
189	  | nil =>
190	    have h0 : divisorOfList ([] : List X.PrimeDivisor) + D₀ = D₀ := by
191	      rw [divisorOfList, zero_add]
192	    rw [h0]
193	    exact Peel.refl k U₀ U₁ D₀
194	  | cons P L ih =>
195	    have hassoc : divisorOfList (P :: L) + D₀ =
196	        pointDivisor P + (divisorOfList L + D₀) := by
197	      rw [divisorOfList]; abel
198	    rw [hassoc]
199	    refine ih.trans k U₀ U₁ (hstep P (divisorOfList L + D₀)) fun Q => ?_
200	    exact le_add_pointDivisor (divisorOfList L + D₀) P Q
201	
202	/-- **Vanishing is a linear-equivalence invariant** (finiteness-free).  The
203	multiplication isomorphism of `ClassInvariance.lean` is a `k`-linear isomorphism
204	`Ȟ¹(D) ≃ₗ[k] Ȟ¹(D')` whenever `D' = D − div g`, and `Subsingleton` transports
205	along any equivalence. -/
206	theorem subsingleton_h1Mod_of_shift {D D' : X.WeilDivisor} {g : X.functionField}
207	    (hg : g ≠ 0)
208	    (hD' : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P =
209	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P - Scheme.RationalMap.order P g)
210	    (h : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D)) :
211	    Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D') :=
212	  (h1ModMulEquiv k U₀ U₁ hg hD').symm.toEquiv.subsingleton
213	
214	/-- **`h¹ = 0` from vanishing**, for consumers phrased on the numerical
215	invariant. -/
216	theorem h1dim_eq_zero_of_subsingleton {D : X.WeilDivisor}
217	    (h : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D)) : h1dim k U₀ U₁ D = 0 := by
218	  rw [h1dim]
219	  exact Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton
220	
221	end Vanishing
222	
223	/-! ## §2. The assembled single-field bound
224	
225	The assembly.  Fix a base divisor `D₀` with `Ȟ¹(D₀) = 0`.  For `D` of large
226	weighted degree the residual class `D − D₀` has `χ ≥ 1`, hence a nonzero global
227	section, hence an **effective** representative `E ~ D − D₀` (the effective-witness
228	dictionary of `ClassInvariance.lean`).  Then `D₀ + E ≥ D₀`, so peeling `E` off the
229	base vanishing kills `Ȟ¹(D₀ + E)`, and `D₀ + E ~ D` transports it to `Ȟ¹(D)`.
230	
231	The threshold that makes the residual class have a section is

307	/-! ## §3. Consequences of the closed ledger
308	
309	The **closed ledger** is the identity `χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D` for every Weil
310	divisor `D`.  In this project it is not a theorem: `chi_telescope_list` proves it
311	for *effective* divisors from a per-step hypothesis which is one application of
312	`chi_add_eq_residueDeg`, and that in turn consumes the ledger's
313	connecting/surjectivity data plus the strong-approximation input `hsurj`.  So the
314	statements below take the closed ledger as an explicit hypothesis, spelled
315	exactly as it will be discharged:
316	
317	`hledger : ∀ D, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D`.
318	
319	That is an honest hypothesis, not a gate class and not a `sorry`: each theorem
320	here says "given the ledger, this follows", and the reader can see what is
321	missing. -/
322	
323	section Ledger
324	
325	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
326	    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
327	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
328	
329	/-- **The ledger holds on list-effective divisors, given the one-point bump.**
330	`chi_telescope_list` computes `χ(Σ_{P ∈ L} P)` as `χ(0) + Σ_{P ∈ L} deg P`, and
331	`degK_divisorOfList` computes `deg_k` of the same divisor as the same sum, so the
332	two agree: `χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D` for `D = divisorOfList L`.
333	
334	This is what pins `degK` as *the* degree of the ledger rather than one weighting
335	among several, and it shows the `hledger` hypothesis of this section is not
336	idle — it holds wherever the one-point bump `hbump` does, which is one application
337	of `chi_add_eq_residueDeg` per step.  What `hbump` still costs is the ledger's
338	connecting/surjectivity data plus the strong-approximation input, and extending
339	from list-effective divisors to *all* divisors additionally needs the negative
340	part; both are why the general ledger is a hypothesis and not a theorem here. -/
341	theorem chi_divisorOfList_eq_degK (L : List X.PrimeDivisor)
342	    (hbump : ∀ (P : X.PrimeDivisor) (E : X.WeilDivisor),
343	      chi k U₀ U₁ (pointDivisor P + E) = chi k U₀ U₁ E + residueDeg k P) :
344	    chi k U₀ U₁ (divisorOfList L) =
345	      chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k (divisorOfList L : X.WeilDivisor) := by
346	  rw [chi_telescope_list k U₀ U₁ L hbump, degK_divisorOfList]
347	
348	/-- **The Riemann inequality in closed weighted form.**  Given the closed ledger,
349	`deg_k D + χ(0) ≤ ℓ(D)` for every `D` — the `h¹ ≥ 0` half applied to the
350	telescoped Euler characteristic.  (This is `Adelic.riemann_inequality` with its
351	`htel` hypothesis supplied from the ledger and the degree pinned to the
352	residue-weighted `deg_k`.) -/
353	theorem degK_add_chi_zero_le_ell
354	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
355	    (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
356	    degK k D + chi k U₀ U₁ 0 ≤ (ell k D : ℤ) :=
357	  riemann_inequality k U₀ U₁ (hledger D)
358	
359	end Ledger
360	
361	section LedgerNoetherian
362	
363	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
364	    [IsNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
365	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
366	
367	/-- **`deg_k D < 0 ⟹ ℓ(D) = 0`** (campaign P4(a)).  Given the closed ledger: a
368	nonzero `f ∈ L(D)` would make `D` linearly equivalent to an effective divisor
369	`E = D + div f` (`exists_effective_linearEquiv_of_ne_zero_mem`); `χ` is a
370	class invariant (`chi_eq_of_linearEquivalence`), so the ledger forces
371	`deg_k E = deg_k D < 0`, contradicting `deg_k E ≥ 0` for effective `E`
372	(`degK_nonneg_of_nonneg`).
373	
374	Note the shape: the hypothesis is on `deg_k`, the *weighted* degree, and the
375	argument runs entirely through the class-invariance of `χ` — no vanishing input,
376	no duality. -/
377	theorem ell_eq_zero_of_degK_neg
378	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)

390	      · exact Submodule.zero_mem _

392	    rw [ell, hbot] at hne

396	  have hchi := chi_eq_of_linearEquivalence k U₀ U₁ hEclass

400	  omega

403	counterpart of the geometric statement `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero`.
404

406	`χ` proved in `ClassInvariance.lean`: `0 − div g` is in the class of `0`, so

408	`deg_k (0 − div g) = 0`, i.e. `deg_k (div g) = 0`.

411	`principal_degree_zero`, which asserts the same for the unweighted degree
412	`Σ_P ord_P g`; see §4. -/
413	theorem degK_principal_eq_zero
414	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)

417	  have hchi := chi_eq_of_principal_shift k U₀ U₁ (0 : X.WeilDivisor) hg
418	  rw [hledger ((0 : X.WeilDivisor) - Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg),

423	linearly equivalent divisors have equal weighted degree — the well-definedness
424	statement the Picard route consumes when it needs "the degree of a class". -/
425	theorem degK_eq_of_linearEquivalence
426	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)

428	    degK k D = degK k D' := by
429	  have hchi := chi_eq_of_linearEquivalence k U₀ U₁ h
430	  rw [hledger D, hledger D'] at hchi

432	
433	end LedgerNoetherian

437	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
438	    [IsNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
439	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
440	
441	/-- **The geometric principal-degree-zero statement, reduced to residue degree
442	one.**  `Σ_P ord_P(g) = 0` follows from the closed ledger together with
443	`[κ(P):k] = 1` on the support of `div g`.
444	
445	This makes the reduction of the open leaf `Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero`
446	machine-checked rather than merely asserted: the *whole* remaining content of that
447	leaf, given the ledger, is the residue-degree-one fact for a smooth proper curve
448	over an algebraically closed field.  It is stated here on the adelic hypotheses
449	(`Algebra k K(X)`, `IsConstantField`, a 2-affine cover, the ledger) rather than on
450	the leaf's own geometric hypotheses, which is why it does not literally close that
451	`sorry` — the missing step is instantiating these hypotheses from
452	`[IsProper] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1] [GeometricallyIrreducible]` over `k̄`,
453	together with `residueDeg k̄ P = 1`. -/
454	theorem degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one
455	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
456	    {g : X.functionField} (hg : g ≠ 0)
457	    (h1 : ∀ P ∈ (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from
458	      Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg).support, residueDeg k P = 1) :
459	    Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree (Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg) = 0 := by
460	  rw [← degK_eq_degree_of_residueDeg_eq_one k h1]

463	end GeometricDegree

465	/-! ## §4. `degK_principal_eq_zero` versus the geometric `principal_degree_zero`
466	
467	`degK_principal_eq_zero` above and the open leaf
468	`Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal_degree_zero` are **different statements**, and the
469	first does not imply the second.  Recorded here because the difference is easy to
470	misread as a formality.
471	
472	* `degK_principal_eq_zero` concerns `deg_k (div g) = Σ_P ord_P(g)·[κ(P):k]`.  Its
473	  proof is the χ-transport of `ClassInvariance.lean` plus the closed ledger, and
474	  it is stated over an **arbitrary** base field of constants `k`.
475	* `principal_degree_zero` concerns the **unweighted** `Σ_P ord_P(g)`, and is
476	  stated on a smooth proper curve over an algebraically **closed** `k̄` with no
477	  field of constants in sight and no ledger hypothesis.
478	
479	Over `k̄` the two degrees coincide because every closed point of a smooth curve has
480	residue field `k̄`, i.e. `[κ(P):k̄] = 1`.  That collapse is
481	`degK_eq_degree_of_residueDeg_eq_one`, and composing it with
482	`degK_principal_eq_zero` gives `degree_principal_eq_zero_of_residueDeg_eq_one`:
483	the **unweighted** statement, proved, from the ledger plus residue-degree-one.
484	
485	So the reduction is now machine-checked, and the residue of the open leaf is
486	exactly two items, neither of them about divisor theory:
487	
488	1. `residueDeg k̄ P = 1` for every prime divisor `P` of a smooth proper curve over
489	   an algebraically closed `k̄` — a statement about residue fields of closed
490	   points (`κ(P)` is a finite extension of `k̄`, hence `k̄`);
491	2. the instance plumbing that places `principal_degree_zero`'s own geometric
492	   hypotheses in adelic shape: an `Algebra k̄ K(C)` with

8	/-!
9	# Adelic Riemann–Roch — bounded `H¹` vanishing over a single base field
10	
11	This file assembles the **single-field bounded vanishing** statement of the
12	campaign's cluster P (P5, primary clause):
13	
14	`∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D, b ≤ deg_k D → Subsingleton (Ȟ¹(D))`
15	
16	from three inputs that are named explicitly in every statement:
17	
18	1. **a base vanishing** `Subsingleton (Ȟ¹(D₀))` at one divisor `D₀`;
19	2. **the peel input** — surjectivity of the twist `Ȟ¹(D) ↠ Ȟ¹(D')` for `D ≤ D'`,
20	   in the concrete form `𝒜(D') = 𝒜(D) + B(D')`.  This is exactly the `htwist`
21	   datum of the χ-ledger (`chi_add`), unwound;
22	3. **the closed ledger** `χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D`, used only to produce an
23	   effective witness in the class of `D − D₀`.
24	
25	Nothing here is a `sorry` and nothing here is a new gate class: each theorem is of
26	the form "given (1)–(3), the bound exists", with `b` computed explicitly as
27	`b = deg_k D₀ + 1 − χ(0)`.
28	
29	## Vanishing as `Subsingleton`, not as `h¹ = 0`
30	
31	Vanishing is stated as `Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D)` rather than
32	`h1dim k U₀ U₁ D = 0`.  The two agree when `Ȟ¹(D)` is finite-dimensional, but the
33	`Subsingleton` form needs **no finiteness instance**, so the vanishing lane stays
34	independent of the finiteness gates.  `h1dim_eq_zero_of_subsingleton` converts.
35	
36	## Main declarations
37	
38	* `subsingleton_h1Mod_iff` — `Ȟ¹(D) = 0 ⟺ 𝒜(D) ⊆ B(D)`: the concrete criterion
39	  everything below runs on.
40	* `subsingleton_h1Mod_peel` — the **peel step**: base vanishing at `D` plus the
41	  peel input transports vanishing to any `D' ≥ D`.
42	* `subsingleton_h1Mod_of_linearEquivalence` — vanishing is a class invariant
43	  (from `ClassInvariance.lean`, finiteness-free).
44	* `exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod` — the assembled bound.
45	
46	## Relation to the sibling project's `UniformVanishing.lean`
47	
48	`AJCR RiemannRoch/UniformVanishing.lean` proves a statement of exactly this
49	shape, `∃ b, ∀ D, b ≤ deg D → Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(D))`, and its proof has the same
50	skeleton: fix a base twist, produce an effective witness of the residual class,
51	peel it, transport along the class.  **This file is not a port of it.**  AJCR's
52	version obtains its base vanishing from the FLV-class machine
53	(`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean`, via a finite dominant `π : Y → ℙ¹` and the fiber
54	divisor) and its peel step from `peel_effective` on `divisorSheaf`; neither the
55	FLV machinery nor `divisorSheaf` exists in AJC.  So here (1) and (2) are named
56	hypotheses rather than discharged lemmas, and the file is honest about that: what
57	is *new* relative to AJC is the assembly and the class-transport, and those are
58	now proved.
59	
60	## The three gaps, kept apart
61	
62	`exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod` is **single-field**: `k`, the cover `U₀, U₁` and
63	the base divisor `D₀` are all fixed.  It is therefore strictly weaker than the two
64	things downstream consumers eventually want, and neither is proved anywhere in
65	this project:
66	
67	* **extension uniformity** — the *same* `b` for every field extension `κ/k`.
68	  Needs flat base change of the bound along `k → κ`; nothing here quantifies over
69	  extensions, and note that even the *statement* needs the base-changed cover
70	  (`RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean` supplies `C_κ` as an AJC curve, but not the
71	  transported 2-affine cover data on which `Ȟ¹` here is pinned).
72	* **global generation** above the bound.  Needs `Ȟ¹(D − x) = 0` at every closed
73	  point `x`, i.e. the bound raised by the maximal residue degree, plus the
74	  evaluation-surjectivity argument.  Not addressed.
75	
76	`ajc-gate` should therefore not read this file as discharging a global-generation
77	or extension-uniform hypothesis; it discharges the single-field bounded-vanishing
78	shape only, and only relative to (1)–(3).
79	-/

101	theorem subsingleton_h1Mod_iff (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
102	    Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D) ↔
103	      sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D ≤ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D := by
104	  constructor
105	  · intro hsub x hx
106	    have hzero : Submodule.Quotient.mk (p := Submodule.comap

108	        (⟨x, hx⟩ : sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
109	    rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero, Submodule.mem_comap,
110	      Submodule.subtype_apply] at hzero
111	    exact hzero
112	  · intro hle
113	    constructor
114	    intro a b
115	    obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ a
116	    obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ b
117	    rw [Submodule.Quotient.eq, Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply]

121	is surjective — concretely, every overlap section of `𝒪(D')` agrees, modulo the
122	coboundary `B(D')`, with an overlap section of `𝒪(D)`.  Then `Ȟ¹(D')` vanishes.
123	
124	`D'` is typically `D + E` with `E ≥ 0`: this is "peel off an effective divisor",
125	the step that turns one base vanishing into vanishing on a whole cone.  The
126	`hpeel` hypothesis is the ledger's surjectivity datum `htwist`, unwound; it is
127	supplied here as a hypothesis because AJC has no unconditional source for it. -/
128	theorem subsingleton_h1Mod_peel {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
129	    (hbase : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D))
130	    (hpeel : ∀ x ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D', ∃ y ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D,
131	      x - y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D')
132	    (hle : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P ≤
133	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) :
134	    Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D') := by
135	  rw [subsingleton_h1Mod_iff] at hbase ⊢
136	  intro x hx
137	  obtain ⟨y, hy, hxy⟩ := hpeel x hx
138	  have hyB : y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D' := by
139	    have : y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D := hbase hy
140	    exact coboundarySub_mono k U₀ U₁ hle this
141	  have : x = (x - y) + y := by abel
142	  rw [this]
143	  exact (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D').add_mem hxy hyB

145	/-- **The peel relation `Peel D D'`.**  "Every overlap section of `𝒪(D')` agrees,
146	modulo the coboundary `B(D')`, with an overlap section of `𝒪(D)`" — equivalently,
147	the twist `Ȟ¹(D) → Ȟ¹(D')` is surjective.  Named so that it can be composed
148	(`Peel.trans`) and so that consumers can discharge it one point at a time rather
149	than in one step. -/
150	def Peel (D D' : X.WeilDivisor) : Prop :=
151	  ∀ x ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D', ∃ y ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D,
152	    x - y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D'

154	/-- **The peel relation is reflexive** (take `y = x`). -/
155	theorem Peel.refl (D : X.WeilDivisor) : Peel k U₀ U₁ D D :=
156	  fun x hx => ⟨x, hx, by simp⟩
157	
158	/-- **The peel relation composes.**  `Peel D₀ D₁` and `Peel D₁ D₂` give
159	`Peel D₀ D₂`, provided `D₁ ≤ D₂` (so that `B(D₁) ⊆ B(D₂)`).

161	This is what makes the peel hypothesis of `exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod`
162	tractable: it need only be established for **one-point** bumps `E ↦ E + P`, then
163	chained along an effective divisor.  Chaining one-point peels is the adelic
164	analogue of AJCR's `peel_effective`, which peels a whole effective divisor in one

166	theorem Peel.trans {D₀ D₁ D₂ : X.WeilDivisor}
167	    (h₀₁ : Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ D₁) (h₁₂ : Peel k U₀ U₁ D₁ D₂)
168	    (hle : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₁) P ≤
169	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₂) P) :
170	    Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ D₂ := by
171	  intro x hx
172	  obtain ⟨y, hy, hxy⟩ := h₁₂ x hx
173	  obtain ⟨z, hz, hyz⟩ := h₀₁ y hy
174	  refine ⟨z, hz, ?_⟩
175	  have : x - z = (x - y) + (y - z) := by abel
176	  rw [this]
177	  exact (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D₂).add_mem hxy
178	    (coboundarySub_mono k U₀ U₁ hle hyz)

181	`Peel E (1·P + E)` for every prime divisor `P` and every `E` — then `D₀` peels to
182	`divisorOfList L + D₀` for every list `L`, i.e. to `D₀` plus an arbitrary effective
183	divisor.  Induction on `L` with `Peel.trans`. -/
184	theorem Peel.of_list (hstep : ∀ (P : X.PrimeDivisor) (E : X.WeilDivisor),
185	      Peel k U₀ U₁ E (pointDivisor P + E))
186	    (D₀ : X.WeilDivisor) (L : List X.PrimeDivisor) :
187	    Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ (divisorOfList L + D₀) := by
188	  induction L with
189	  | nil =>
190	    have h0 : divisorOfList ([] : List X.PrimeDivisor) + D₀ = D₀ := by
191	      rw [divisorOfList, zero_add]
192	    rw [h0]
193	    exact Peel.refl k U₀ U₁ D₀
194	  | cons P L ih =>
195	    have hassoc : divisorOfList (P :: L) + D₀ =
196	        pointDivisor P + (divisorOfList L + D₀) := by
197	      rw [divisorOfList]; abel
198	    rw [hassoc]
199	    refine ih.trans k U₀ U₁ (hstep P (divisorOfList L + D₀)) fun Q => ?_
200	    exact le_add_pointDivisor (divisorOfList L + D₀) P Q

303	    exists_effective_linearEquiv_of_le_degK k U₀ U₁ hledger
304	      (D := D - D₀) (by rw [degK_sub]; omega)
305	  -- `D₀ + E ≥ D₀`, so peeling `E` off the base vanishing kills `Ȟ¹(D₀ + E)`
306	  have hmono : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₀) P ≤
307	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₀ + E) P := by
308	    intro P
309	    rw [show (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₀ + E) P =
310	          (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₀) P +
311	            (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E) P from Finsupp.add_apply _ _ _]
312	    have := hEnonneg P
313	    linarith
314	  have hpeeled : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ (D₀ + E)) :=
315	    subsingleton_h1Mod_peel k U₀ U₁ hbase (hpeel (D₀ + E) hmono) hmono
316	  -- `D₀ + E ~ D₀ + (D - D₀) = D`, so transport along the class
317	  obtain ⟨g, hg, hgE⟩ := hEclass
318	  have hshift : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P =
319	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₀ + E) P - Scheme.RationalMap.order P g := by
320	    intro P
321	    have hDsub : D = (D₀ + E) - Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg := by
322	      have : E = (D - D₀) + Scheme.WeilDivisor.principal g hg := by
323	        rw [← hgE]; abel
324	      rw [this]; abel
325	    rw [hDsub]
326	    exact sub_principal_apply hg P
327	  exact subsingleton_h1Mod_of_shift k U₀ U₁ hg hshift hpeeled
328

330	/-- **Every effective divisor is list-effective.**  An effective `E ≥ 0` is
331	`Σ_{P ∈ L} 1·P` for some list `L` of prime divisors, multiplicity encoded by
332	repetition.  Strong induction on the support: peel one support point `P₀`, replace
333	`E` by `E − 1·P₀` (whose support is contained in that of `E`, and strictly smaller
334	when `E(P₀) = 1`), recurse.
335	
336	Implemented as induction on `(Σ_P E(P)).toNat`, which strictly decreases at each
337	peel because `E(P₀) ≥ 1` and every other coefficient is unchanged.  This discharges
338	the list-effectivity bookkeeping of
339	`exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod_of_pointPeel`.  Pure `Finsupp` combinatorics — the
340	geometric instances play no role, hence the `omit`. -/
341	theorem exists_divisorOfList_of_nonneg (E : X.WeilDivisor)
342	    (hE : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, 0 ≤ (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E) P) :
343	    ∃ L : List X.PrimeDivisor, E = divisorOfList L := by
344	  classical
345	  -- induct on the total (unweighted) mass of `E`
346	  generalize hn : (Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree E).toNat = n
347	  induction n generalizing E with
348	  | zero =>
349	    -- total mass 0 with all coefficients ≥ 0 forces `E = 0`
350	    refine ⟨[], ?_⟩
351	    rw [divisorOfList]
352	    have hsum : (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E).sum (fun _ n => n) = 0 := by
353	      have hnn : 0 ≤ Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree E :=
354	        Finset.sum_nonneg fun P _ => hE P
355	      have hdeg : Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree E
356	          = (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E).sum (fun _ n => n) := rfl
357	      omega
358	    -- a nonnegative finsupp of total mass 0 is zero
359	    apply Finsupp.ext
360	    intro P
361	    by_cases hP : P ∈ (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E).support
362	    · have := Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg
363	        (f := fun Q => (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E) Q)
364	        (s := (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E).support)
365	        (fun Q _ => hE Q)
366	      have hzero := (this.mp hsum) P hP
367	      rw [show (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from (0 : X.WeilDivisor)) P = (0 : ℤ) from
368	        Finsupp.zero_apply]
369	      exact hzero
370	    · rw [Finsupp.notMem_support_iff] at hP
371	      rw [show (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from (0 : X.WeilDivisor)) P = (0 : ℤ) from
372	        Finsupp.zero_apply]
373	      exact hP
374	  | succ n ih =>
375	    -- positive mass: some coefficient is ≥ 1
376	    have hdegE : Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree E
377	        = (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E).sum (fun _ n => n) := rfl
378	    have hpos : 0 < (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E).sum (fun _ n => n) := by omega
379	    obtain ⟨P₀, hP₀supp, hP₀pos⟩ :
380	        ∃ P₀ ∈ (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E).support,
381	          0 < (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E) P₀ := by
382	      by_contra hno
383	      push Not at hno
384	      have hle0 : (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E).sum (fun _ n => n) ≤ 0 :=
385	        Finset.sum_nonpos fun Q hQ => hno Q hQ
386	      omega
387	    -- peel `1·P₀`
388	    set E' : X.WeilDivisor := E - pointDivisor P₀ with hE'def
389	    have hE'apply : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor,
390	        (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E') P =
391	          (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E) P -
392	            (if P = P₀ then 1 else 0) := by
393	      intro P
394	      rw [hE'def, show (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E - pointDivisor P₀) P =
395	            (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E) P -
396	              (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from pointDivisor P₀) P from
397	          Finsupp.sub_apply _ _ _, pointDivisor]
398	      by_cases h : P = P₀
399	      · rw [h, Finsupp.single_eq_same, if_pos rfl]
400	      · rw [Finsupp.single_eq_of_ne (Ne.symm (Ne.symm h) : P ≠ P₀), if_neg h]
401	    have hE'nonneg : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor,
402	        0 ≤ (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E') P := by
403	      intro P
404	      rw [hE'apply P]
405	      by_cases h : P = P₀
406	      · subst h; rw [if_pos rfl]; omega
407	      · rw [if_neg h]; have := hE P; omega
408	    -- the mass drops by exactly one
409	    have hmass : Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree E'
410	        = Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree E - 1 := by
411	      have hEE' : E = E' + pointDivisor P₀ := by rw [hE'def]; abel
412	      have hadd := Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree_add E' (pointDivisor P₀)
413	      have hpt : Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree (pointDivisor P₀ : X.WeilDivisor) = 1 := by
414	        rw [Scheme.WeilDivisor.degree, pointDivisor]
415	        exact Finsupp.sum_single_index rfl
416	      rw [hpt, ← hEE'] at hadd
417	      omega
418	    obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ := ih E' hE'nonneg (by omega)
419	    refine ⟨P₀ :: L, ?_⟩
420	    rw [divisorOfList, ← hL, hE'def]
421	    abel
422	
423	/-- **The bound from the one-point peel** — the form a consumer should actually
424	aim at.  Instead of the peel input for all `D' ≥ D₀` at once, it suffices to have
425	it for a **single point bump** `E ↦ 1·P + E`, uniformly in `P` and `E`: chaining
426	along a list (`Peel.of_list`) recovers the general case.
427	
428	So the hypotheses reduce to exactly three, and only two of them are open
429	mathematics: the base vanishing, the **one-point** peel, and the closed ledger.
430	The list-effectivity bookkeeping is discharged internally by
431	`exists_divisorOfList_of_nonneg`. -/
432	theorem exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod_of_pointPeel
433	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
434	    (D₀ : X.WeilDivisor) (hbase : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D₀))
435	    (hstep : ∀ (P : X.PrimeDivisor) (E : X.WeilDivisor),
436	      Peel k U₀ U₁ E (pointDivisor P + E)) :
437	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, b ≤ degK k D →
438	      Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D) := by
439	  refine exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod k U₀ U₁ hledger D₀ hbase ?_
440	  -- the general peel input, recovered from the one-point one
441	  intro D' hmono
442	  -- `D' = D₀ + (D' - D₀)` with `D' - D₀` effective, hence list-effective
443	  have hEnonneg : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor,
444	      0 ≤ (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D' - D₀) P := by
445	    intro P
446	    rw [show (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D' - D₀) P =
447	          (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P -
448	            (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₀) P from Finsupp.sub_apply _ _ _]
449	    have := hmono P
450	    linarith
451	  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ := exists_divisorOfList_of_nonneg (D' - D₀) hEnonneg
452	  have hD' : D' = divisorOfList L + D₀ := by rw [← hL]; abel
453	  rw [hD']
454	  exact Peel.of_list k U₀ U₁ hstep D₀ L
455	
456	/-- **The bound in numerical form.**  Same statement with the conclusion read on
457	`h¹` rather than on `Subsingleton`; `h1dim` is `0` for a subsingleton without any
458	finiteness input (`Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton`). -/
459	theorem exists_bound_h1dim_eq_zero
460	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
461	    (D₀ : X.WeilDivisor) (hbase : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D₀))
462	    (hpeel : ∀ D' : X.WeilDivisor,
463	      (∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₀) P ≤
464	        (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) →
465	      ∀ x ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D', ∃ y ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D₀,
466	        x - y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D') :
467	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, b ≤ degK k D → h1dim k U₀ U₁ D = 0 := by
468	  obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ :=
469	    exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod k U₀ U₁ hledger D₀ hbase hpeel
470	  exact ⟨b, fun D hD => h1dim_eq_zero_of_subsingleton k U₀ U₁ (hb D hD)⟩
471	
472	/-- **Above the bound, `ℓ` is computed exactly by the ledger:**
473	`ℓ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D`.  This is the Riemann–Roch conclusion in the vanishing
474	range — the shape a Grassmannian-embedding or rank-counting consumer wants, since
475	it turns `ℓ` from an inequality into a formula. -/
476	theorem ell_eq_of_bound
477	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
478	    {D : X.WeilDivisor} (hvan : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D)) :
479	    (ell k D : ℤ) = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D := by
480	  have hh1 := h1dim_eq_zero_of_subsingleton k U₀ U₁ hvan
481	  have := hledger D
482	  rw [chi, hh1] at this
483	  omega
484	
485	end Bound

def LinearEquivalence [IsIntegral X] [IsNoetherian X]
    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X] (D D' : X.WeilDivisor) : Prop :=
  ∃ (f : X.functionField) (hf : f ≠ 0), D - D' = principal f hf

1	/-

3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Adelic.SectionBounds
7	
8	/-!
9	# Adelic Riemann–Roch — bounded `H¹` vanishing over a single base field
10	
11	This file assembles the **single-field bounded vanishing** statement of the
12	campaign's cluster P (P5, primary clause):
13	
14	`∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D, b ≤ deg_k D → Subsingleton (Ȟ¹(D))`
15	
16	from three inputs that are named explicitly in every statement:
17	
18	1. **a base vanishing** `Subsingleton (Ȟ¹(D₀))` at one divisor `D₀`;
19	2. **the peel input** — surjectivity of the twist `Ȟ¹(D) ↠ Ȟ¹(D')` for `D ≤ D'`,
20	   in the concrete form `𝒜(D') = 𝒜(D) + B(D')`.  This is exactly the `htwist`
21	   datum of the χ-ledger (`chi_add`), unwound;
22	3. **the closed ledger** `χ(D) = χ(0) + deg_k D`, used only to produce an
23	   effective witness in the class of `D − D₀`.
24	
25	Nothing here is a `sorry` and nothing here is a new gate class: each theorem is of
26	the form "given (1)–(3), the bound exists", with `b` computed explicitly as
27	`b = deg_k D₀ + 1 − χ(0)`.
28	
29	## Vanishing as `Subsingleton`, not as `h¹ = 0`
30	
31	Vanishing is stated as `Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D)` rather than
32	`h1dim k U₀ U₁ D = 0`.  The two agree when `Ȟ¹(D)` is finite-dimensional, but the
33	`Subsingleton` form needs **no finiteness instance**, so the vanishing lane stays
34	independent of the finiteness gates.  `h1dim_eq_zero_of_subsingleton` converts.
35	
36	## Main declarations
37	
38	* `subsingleton_h1Mod_iff` — `Ȟ¹(D) = 0 ⟺ 𝒜(D) ⊆ B(D)`: the concrete criterion
39	  everything below runs on.
40	* `subsingleton_h1Mod_peel` — the **peel step**: base vanishing at `D` plus the
41	  peel input transports vanishing to any `D' ≥ D`.
42	* `subsingleton_h1Mod_of_linearEquivalence` — vanishing is a class invariant
43	  (from `ClassInvariance.lean`, finiteness-free).
44	* `exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod` — the assembled bound.
45	
46	## Relation to the sibling project's `UniformVanishing.lean`
47	
48	`AJCR RiemannRoch/UniformVanishing.lean` proves a statement of exactly this
49	shape, `∃ b, ∀ D, b ≤ deg D → Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(D))`, and its proof has the same
50	skeleton: fix a base twist, produce an effective witness of the residual class,
51	peel it, transport along the class.  **This file is not a port of it.**  AJCR's
52	version obtains its base vanishing from the FLV-class machine
53	(`RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean`, via a finite dominant `π : Y → ℙ¹` and the fiber
54	divisor) and its peel step from `peel_effective` on `divisorSheaf`; neither the
55	FLV machinery nor `divisorSheaf` exists in AJC.  So here (1) and (2) are named
56	hypotheses rather than discharged lemmas, and the file is honest about that: what
57	is *new* relative to AJC is the assembly and the class-transport, and those are
58	now proved.
59	
60	## The three gaps, kept apart
61	
62	`exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod` is **single-field**: `k`, the cover `U₀, U₁` and
63	the base divisor `D₀` are all fixed.  It is therefore strictly weaker than the two
64	things downstream consumers eventually want, and neither is proved anywhere in
65	this project:
66	
67	* **extension uniformity** — the *same* `b` for every field extension `κ/k`.
68	  Needs flat base change of the bound along `k → κ`; nothing here quantifies over
69	  extensions, and note that even the *statement* needs the base-changed cover
70	  (`RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange.lean` supplies `C_κ` as an AJC curve, but not the
71	  transported 2-affine cover data on which `Ȟ¹` here is pinned).
72	* **global generation** above the bound.  Needs `Ȟ¹(D − x) = 0` at every closed
73	  point `x`, i.e. the bound raised by the maximal residue degree, plus the
74	  evaluation-surjectivity argument.  Not addressed.
75	
76	`ajc-gate` should therefore not read this file as discharging a global-generation
77	or extension-uniform hypothesis; it discharges the single-field bounded-vanishing
78	shape only, and only relative to (1)–(3).
79	-/
80	
81	set_option autoImplicit false
82	
83	universe u
84	
85	open CategoryTheory Limits IsDedekindDomain
86	open scoped WithZero
87	
88	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
89	namespace Adelic
90	
91	section Vanishing
92	
93	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
94	    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
95	    [Algebra k X.functionField] [IsConstantField k X] (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
96	
97	/-- **The concrete vanishing criterion.**  `Ȟ¹(D) = 𝒜(D)/B(D)` is trivial exactly
98	when the overlap sections are already coboundaries: `𝒜(D) ⊆ B(D)`.  (The reverse
99	inclusion always holds, `coboundarySub_le_overlap`, so the condition really is
100	equality.) -/
101	theorem subsingleton_h1Mod_iff (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
102	    Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D) ↔
103	      sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D ≤ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D := by
104	  constructor
105	  · intro hsub x hx
106	    have hzero : Submodule.Quotient.mk (p := Submodule.comap
107	        (sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D).subtype (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D))
108	        (⟨x, hx⟩ : sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) = 0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _
109	    rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero, Submodule.mem_comap,
110	      Submodule.subtype_apply] at hzero
111	    exact hzero
112	  · intro hle
113	    constructor
114	    intro a b
115	    obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ a
116	    obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ b
117	    rw [Submodule.Quotient.eq, Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply]
118	    exact hle ((sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D).sub_mem x.2 y.2)

120	/-- **The peel step.**  Suppose `Ȟ¹(D)` vanishes and the twist `Ȟ¹(D) → Ȟ¹(D')`
121	is surjective — concretely, every overlap section of `𝒪(D')` agrees, modulo the
122	coboundary `B(D')`, with an overlap section of `𝒪(D)`.  Then `Ȟ¹(D')` vanishes.
123	
124	`D'` is typically `D + E` with `E ≥ 0`: this is "peel off an effective divisor",
125	the step that turns one base vanishing into vanishing on a whole cone.  The
126	`hpeel` hypothesis is the ledger's surjectivity datum `htwist`, unwound; it is
127	supplied here as a hypothesis because AJC has no unconditional source for it. -/
128	theorem subsingleton_h1Mod_peel {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
129	    (hbase : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D))
130	    (hpeel : ∀ x ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D', ∃ y ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D,
131	      x - y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D')
132	    (hle : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P ≤
133	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) :
134	    Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D') := by
135	  rw [subsingleton_h1Mod_iff] at hbase ⊢
136	  intro x hx
137	  obtain ⟨y, hy, hxy⟩ := hpeel x hx
138	  have hyB : y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D' := by
139	    have : y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D := hbase hy
140	    exact coboundarySub_mono k U₀ U₁ hle this
141	  have : x = (x - y) + y := by abel
142	  rw [this]
143	  exact (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D').add_mem hxy hyB
144	
145	/-- **The peel relation `Peel D D'`.**  "Every overlap section of `𝒪(D')` agrees,
146	modulo the coboundary `B(D')`, with an overlap section of `𝒪(D)`" — equivalently,
147	the twist `Ȟ¹(D) → Ȟ¹(D')` is surjective.  Named so that it can be composed
148	(`Peel.trans`) and so that consumers can discharge it one point at a time rather
149	than in one step. -/
150	def Peel (D D' : X.WeilDivisor) : Prop :=
151	  ∀ x ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D', ∃ y ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D,
152	    x - y ∈ coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D'

154	/-- **The peel relation is reflexive** (take `y = x`). -/
155	theorem Peel.refl (D : X.WeilDivisor) : Peel k U₀ U₁ D D :=
156	  fun x hx => ⟨x, hx, by simp⟩
157	
158	/-- **The peel relation composes.**  `Peel D₀ D₁` and `Peel D₁ D₂` give
159	`Peel D₀ D₂`, provided `D₁ ≤ D₂` (so that `B(D₁) ⊆ B(D₂)`).

161	This is what makes the peel hypothesis of `exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod`
162	tractable: it need only be established for **one-point** bumps `E ↦ E + P`, then
163	chained along an effective divisor.  Chaining one-point peels is the adelic
164	analogue of AJCR's `peel_effective`, which peels a whole effective divisor in one
165	sheaf-level step. -/
166	theorem Peel.trans {D₀ D₁ D₂ : X.WeilDivisor}
167	    (h₀₁ : Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ D₁) (h₁₂ : Peel k U₀ U₁ D₁ D₂)
168	    (hle : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₁) P ≤
169	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₂) P) :
170	    Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ D₂ := by
171	  intro x hx
172	  obtain ⟨y, hy, hxy⟩ := h₁₂ x hx
173	  obtain ⟨z, hz, hyz⟩ := h₀₁ y hy
174	  refine ⟨z, hz, ?_⟩
175	  have : x - z = (x - y) + (y - z) := by abel
176	  rw [this]
177	  exact (coboundarySub k U₀ U₁ D₂).add_mem hxy
178	    (coboundarySub_mono k U₀ U₁ hle hyz)

180	/-- **Chaining one-point peels along a list.**  If every one-point bump peels —
181	`Peel E (1·P + E)` for every prime divisor `P` and every `E` — then `D₀` peels to
182	`divisorOfList L + D₀` for every list `L`, i.e. to `D₀` plus an arbitrary effective
183	divisor.  Induction on `L` with `Peel.trans`. -/
184	theorem Peel.of_list (hstep : ∀ (P : X.PrimeDivisor) (E : X.WeilDivisor),
185	      Peel k U₀ U₁ E (pointDivisor P + E))
186	    (D₀ : X.WeilDivisor) (L : List X.PrimeDivisor) :
187	    Peel k U₀ U₁ D₀ (divisorOfList L + D₀) := by
188	  induction L with
189	  | nil =>
190	    have h0 : divisorOfList ([] : List X.PrimeDivisor) + D₀ = D₀ := by
191	      rw [divisorOfList, zero_add]
192	    rw [h0]
193	    exact Peel.refl k U₀ U₁ D₀
194	  | cons P L ih =>
195	    have hassoc : divisorOfList (P :: L) + D₀ =
196	        pointDivisor P + (divisorOfList L + D₀) := by
197	      rw [divisorOfList]; abel
198	    rw [hassoc]
199	    refine ih.trans k U₀ U₁ (hstep P (divisorOfList L + D₀)) fun Q => ?_
200	    exact le_add_pointDivisor (divisorOfList L + D₀) P Q
201	
202	/-- **Vanishing is a linear-equivalence invariant** (finiteness-free).  The
203	multiplication isomorphism of `ClassInvariance.lean` is a `k`-linear isomorphism
204	`Ȟ¹(D) ≃ₗ[k] Ȟ¹(D')` whenever `D' = D − div g`, and `Subsingleton` transports
205	along any equivalence. -/
206	theorem subsingleton_h1Mod_of_shift {D D' : X.WeilDivisor} {g : X.functionField}
207	    (hg : g ≠ 0)
208	    (hD' : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P =
209	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P - Scheme.RationalMap.order P g)
210	    (h : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D)) :
211	    Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D') :=
212	  (h1ModMulEquiv k U₀ U₁ hg hD').symm.toEquiv.subsingleton
213	
214	/-- **`h¹ = 0` from vanishing**, for consumers phrased on the numerical
215	invariant. -/
216	theorem h1dim_eq_zero_of_subsingleton {D : X.WeilDivisor}
217	    (h : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D)) : h1dim k U₀ U₁ D = 0 := by
218	  rw [h1dim]
219	  exact Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton
220	
221	end Vanishing

223	/-! ## §2. The assembled single-field bound
224	
225	The assembly.  Fix a base divisor `D₀` with `Ȟ¹(D₀) = 0`.  For `D` of large
226	weighted degree the residual class `D − D₀` has `χ ≥ 1`, hence a nonzero global
227	section, hence an **effective** representative `E ~ D − D₀` (the effective-witness
228	dictionary of `ClassInvariance.lean`).  Then `D₀ + E ≥ D₀`, so peeling `E` off the
229	base vanishing kills `Ȟ¹(D₀ + E)`, and `D₀ + E ~ D` transports it to `Ȟ¹(D)`.
230	
231	The threshold that makes the residual class have a section is
232	`b := deg_k D₀ + 1 − χ(0)`: for `deg_k D ≥ b` the ledger gives
233	`χ(D − D₀) = χ(0) + deg_k D − deg_k D₀ ≥ 1`, and `χ ≤ ℓ` does the rest.

238	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]

244	`Γ(⊤, 𝒪(D)) ≠ 0`. -/
245	theorem exists_ne_zero_mem_of_one_le_chi {D : X.WeilDivisor}
246	    (hchi : 1 ≤ chi k U₀ U₁ D) :
247	    ∃ f : X.functionField, f ∈ sectionSub k ⊤ D ∧ f ≠ 0 := by
248	  have hell : 1 ≤ (ell k D : ℤ) := le_trans hchi (chi_le_ell k U₀ U₁ D)
249	  by_contra hno
250	  have hbot : sectionSub k ⊤ D = ⊥ := by
251	    apply le_antisymm _ bot_le
252	    intro x hx
253	    rcases eq_or_ne x 0 with rfl | hx0
254	    · exact Submodule.zero_mem _
255	    · exact absurd ⟨x, hx, hx0⟩ hno
256	  rw [ell, hbot] at hell
257	  simp at hell

262	`exists_effective_of_picClass`, proved here from `χ ≤ ℓ` plus the effective-witness

265	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
266	    {D : X.WeilDivisor} (hdeg : 1 - chi k U₀ U₁ 0 ≤ degK k D) :
267	    ∃ E : X.WeilDivisor,
268	      (∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, 0 ≤ (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E) P) ∧
269	        Scheme.WeilDivisor.LinearEquivalence E D := by
270	  have hchi : 1 ≤ chi k U₀ U₁ D := by rw [hledger D]; omega
271	  obtain ⟨f, hfmem, hfne⟩ := exists_ne_zero_mem_of_one_le_chi k U₀ U₁ hchi

275	strongest form reachable in AJC today).
276	
277	Given
278	* a base divisor `D₀` with `Ȟ¹(D₀) = 0`,
279	* the **peel input** at `D₀`: for every `D' ≥ D₀`, each overlap section of
280	  `𝒪(D')` agrees modulo `B(D')` with an overlap section of `𝒪(D₀)` — i.e. the
281	  twist `Ȟ¹(D₀) → Ȟ¹(D')` is surjective (the ledger's `htwist` datum, unwound),

288	extensions and says **nothing** about global generation — see the module

290	theorem exists_bound_subsingleton_h1Mod
291	    (hledger : ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, chi k U₀ U₁ D = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + degK k D)
292	    (D₀ : X.WeilDivisor) (hbase : Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D₀))
293	    (hpeel : ∀ D' : X.WeilDivisor,
294	      (∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₀) P ≤
295	        (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) →
296	      ∀ x ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D', ∃ y ∈ sectionSub k (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D₀,

298	    ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ D : X.WeilDivisor, b ≤ degK k D →
299	      Subsingleton (H1Mod k U₀ U₁ D) := by
300	  refine ⟨degK k D₀ + 1 - chi k U₀ U₁ 0, fun D hD => ?_⟩
301	  -- the residual class `D - D₀` has weighted degree ≥ 1 - χ(0), so it is effective
302	  obtain ⟨E, hEnonneg, hEclass⟩ :=
303	    exists_effective_linearEquiv_of_le_degK k U₀ U₁ hledger
304	      (D := D - D₀) (by rw [degK_sub]; omega)
305	  -- `D₀ + E ≥ D₀`, so peeling `E` off the base vanishing kills `Ȟ¹(D₀ + E)`

308	    intro P

310	          (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D₀) P +
311	            (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E) P from Finsupp.add_apply _ _ _]

324	      rw [this]; abel

326	    exact sub_principal_apply hg P
